correctness.rationale: For each summand W_S, an isolate in S contributes zero since k≥2 and S is connected whenever W_S is nonzero. Given the data determining W_S, any v outside S has probability (1−p)^(n−k−1) of being isolated on the event used by W_S: the edges to S are already absent and the remaining edges are independent. This gives E[IT]=(n−k)(1−p)^(n−k−1)E[T], including n−k=1. Subtracting E[I]E[T] gives the claimed sign and its unique root for positive E[T]. For t=k/n the function −log(1−t)/t=∫₀¹(1−ts)⁻¹ds is strictly increasing, giving the threshold ordering. Expanding its exponential gives the fixed-k and proportional-size limits; at k=n−1 the exponent is log(n)/(n−1), giving the final scale. The bundled verify.py was inspected, not run; it checks the 60 finite graph comparisons but does not contain the additional threshold stress tests described in the notes. None of the general conclusions depends on these tests.

evidence: Under the permutation-invariant G(n,p) law, replacing T by its average over vertex relabelings preserves E[T] and E[IT] because I is invariant. The averaged statistic is a nonnegative linear combination of the unlabelled component-type counts C_K on k vertices, since the averaging makes the internal weights the same for every occurrence of each type. All C_K have the same covariance multiplier from 00c844d9af13.

Permutation averaging and linearity extend it to exactly the asserted arbitrary internal weights, even when the weights are label dependent. Ordering and scales are routine consequences of that same threshold and do not constitute an independent result.
